question: A consultant is setting up a Claude Project for a client engagement she will work on every week for months. Which two things belong in that set-up? Select two.
options: A) Project knowledge holding the client documents that each chat in the Project should draw on.
B) One chat for each client document, so every document keeps its own conversation thread.
C) Project instructions covering the tone, role and house rules every chat there should follow.
D) A note asking Claude to remember these client details for later use in her unrelated Projects.
E) One very long opening message that every later chat is expected to scroll back through.
correct_answers: A) Project knowledge holding the client documents that each chat in the Project should draw on.
C) Project instructions covering the tone, role and house rules every chat there should follow.
explanations: Correct. Project knowledge is where background documents live so Claude has them in every chat in that Project.
Incorrect. Splitting one document per chat fragments the engagement and abandons the shared knowledge base a Project provides.
Correct. Project instructions are the durable, project-scoped direction that shapes tone, role and house rules across every chat there.
Incorrect. A Project is self-contained, so its context does not spread into other Projects, and asking for that does not create it.
Incorrect. A long opening message is a one-off prompt in one chat, not durable configuration for the Project.
